2 مهّد , inf. n. تَمْهِيدٌ, (tropical:) He adjusted, or arranged, an affair, (S, A, L, Msb, K,) and made it plain, (A, Msb,) and easy. (Msb.) See 1. ―
-b2- مهّد نَفْسَهُ لِفِعْلِ الأَمْرِ (assumed tropical:) He disposed and subjected his mind, or himself, to do the thing. (S, * K, * Msb, art. وطن.) ―
-b3- مهّد, inf. n. تَمْهِيدٌ, (tropical:) He accepted, or admitted, an excuse. (S, L, Msb, K.) You say, مَهَّدْتُ لَهُ العُذْرَ (tropical:) I accepted, or admitted, his excuse. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
